title: AgendaView and EventDetail render calendar meetingUrl into an anchor href with no scheme check (AskPage already guards with safeHttpUrl)
evidence: apps/web/src/pages/calendar/AgendaView.tsx:72 `<a href={m.meetingUrl} target="_blank">` and EventDetail.tsx:49 `href={event.meetingUrl}`. meetingUrl comes from apps/api/src/gws-calendar.ts meetingUrlOf (hangoutLink or conferenceData.entryPoints[video].uri) and the API only length-checks it (text(meetingUrl, 8192)), so any scheme passes through. A javascript: URI would run in the app origin on click and could read localStorage lkbApiKey. Severity is medium, not high, because exploitability is UNCONFIRMED: it is not established that Google Calendar lets an external organizer set a non-http(s) conferenceData uri (Google may normalise or reject it), the victim must click Join, and target=_blank with a javascript: URI is blocked or opened in a blank context by some browsers. Impact if reachable is credential theft, so the fix is applied as defence in depth.
reproduction:
Render <EventDetail event={{...base, meetingUrl: 'javascript:alert(document.domain)'}} /> (or AgendaView with meetings=[{meetingUrl:'javascript:alert(1)'}]). Actual: an <a href="javascript:alert(document.domain)" data-testid="detail-join-link"> is rendered. Expected: no anchor with that href; the text is shown inert. Also hostile forms: ' javascript:x', '	javascript:x', 'JaVaScRiPt:x', 'java
script:x', 'data:text/html,x', 'vbscript:x', '//evil.example/x', 'not a url'.
fix_direction: Shared safeHttpUrl util (http/https only), applied at both call sites; non-http(s) renders as plain text.

title: AuthContext 401 handler still logs out a tab that holds a NEWER key B when storage is empty or unwritable and a late 401 for old key A arrives (the 'storage empty' relevance clause matches any failed key)
evidence: apps/web/src/auth/AuthContext.tsx handleAuthInvalidated: `if (detail.apiKey !== apiKey && detail.apiKey !== storageKey && storageKey !== null) return;` - when storageKey is null the guard falls through whatever the failed key was, so `setApiKeyState(null)` runs although detail.apiKey (A) is not this tab's key (B). client.ts invalidateAuth already removed storage for the key it failed, so the empty-storage clause is not needed for the stored===failed case (that case is covered by detail.apiKey === apiKey). Reachable when localStorage.setItem throws (blocked/private storage: B lives only in memory, storage stays empty) or when another tab signed out (storage cleared). Impact: availability only (tab returns to the login prompt, B must be re-pasted); no wrong key is sent and no data stays on screen.
reproduction: Checker probe (vitest, real AuthProvider + LoginGate): (1) vi.spyOn(Storage.prototype,'setItem').mockImplementation(()=>{throw new Error('x')}); render <AuthProvider><LoginGate><Probe/></LoginGate></AuthProvider>; type 'B' in the API key input and click Continue (key shows B); dispatch new CustomEvent('lkb:auth-invalidated',{detail:{apiKey:'A'}}). Actual: tab goes to the login prompt (key B -> none). Expected: tab keeps B. (2) With working storage: localStorage A; sign out via clearApiKey; log in B; localStorage.clear() (other tab signed out); dispatch the same event for A. Actual: logged out, storage null. Expected: tab keeps B. Control that does pass: storage working and holding B, late 401 for A -> B stays, tab stays logged in.
fix_direction: Make the handler relevant only when detail.apiKey === this tab's current apiKey (state captured at render); drop the storage-empty and stored-key clauses. Keep compare-and-clear on storage. Add AuthContext tests for state B + empty storage and state B + throwing setItem, each with a late 401 for A.
